user.title: Set up Swisspower DynPreis
user.description: Choose how the dynamic tariffs are requested: by tariff name, or with a metering code and an authentication token.

data_description.api_url: Leave the default unless your supplier publishes on a different endpoint.

metering.title: Authentication token
metering.description: Enter your metering code and authentication token.

data_description.tariff_types: One set of entities per selected type, and one API request per type per fetch. Only the price entities are enabled by default; the timestamp, on/off and diagnostic ones are created disabled and can be switched on individually.

tariff_name.title: Tariff name
tariff_name.description: Enter the tariff name (for example D1).

data_description.tariff_types: One set of entities per selected type, and one API request per type per fetch. Only the price entities are enabled by default; the timestamp, on/off and diagnostic ones are created disabled and can be switched on individually.

schedule.title: Fetch times
schedule.description: The API is queried three times a day, each time for a window covering today and the next three days. These times can be changed later in the options.

data_description.update_time: The first fetch of the day.
data_description.update_time_pm: Most suppliers publish tomorrow's prices in the afternoon. While they are still missing after this time, the integration keeps asking at growing intervals.
data_description.update_time_evening: An extra fetch for suppliers that publish late.

error.invalid_url: That is not a valid URL. It has to start with http:// or https://.

init.title: Swisspower DynPreis options
init.description: The API is queried at the three fetch times, each time for a window covering today and the next three days. Most suppliers only publish tomorrow's prices in the afternoon; while they are still missing, the integration asks again at growing intervals after fetch time 2. The "Refresh now" button fetches immediately, outside this schedule.

data.vat_tariff_types: Add VAT to these tariff types

data_description.update_time: The first fetch of the day.
data_description.update_time_pm: Most suppliers publish tomorrow's prices in the afternoon. While they are still missing after this time, the integration keeps asking at growing intervals.
data_description.update_time_evening: An extra fetch for suppliers that publish late.
data_description.vat_rate: The API publishes net prices. This rate is added on top of every price, statistic and chart attribute. Leave it at 0 to show the prices exactly as the supplier sends them.
data_description.vat_entity: Read the rate from this entity's state instead - an input_number, a number or a sensor holding the percentage. Useful when the rate changes: one entity write instead of a reconfiguration. While the entity has no usable state the last rate read from it stays in force, and before it ever had one the fixed rate above applies.
data_description.vat_tariff_types: Feed-in is left out by default: it is a credit to you, not a purchase, so a household that is not registered for VAT does not add it there.
data_description.query_year: For testing only: rewrites the year the API is asked for. Leave empty for normal operation.
